name: CrowdStrike
description: CrowdStrike sells cloud-delivered cybersecurity: a single software agent on customer computers and servers (the Falcon platform) that detects attacks, plus add-on modules for cloud security, identity, log analytics and managed response. It has more than 88,000 customer organizations (January 31, 2026) and 32 modules. Customers pay an annual subscription; 95% of FY2026 revenue was subscription. Its key metric is annual recurring revenue (ARR): $5.84B at July 31, 2026, +25%. A newer 'Falcon Flex' contract lets a customer commit a dollar amount and switch between modules; Flex accounts had $2.29B of ARR (+101%). On July 19, 2024 a faulty CrowdStrike update crashed millions of Windows machines; it still incurs legal and remediation costs. Four-for-one stock split effective July 2, 2026.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recalled from the standard scheme and uncertain; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source.

businessLines.name: Subscription
businessLines.how: Annual per-endpoint or per-module subscriptions billed mostly in advance; growth comes from selling more modules to existing customers and from Falcon Flex commitments. Dollar-based net retention was 115% at January 31, 2026.

revenue.note: Q2 FY2027 subscription revenue $1.40B (+27%); Q1 FY2027 $1.32B (+26%)

businessLines.revenueNote: Q2 FY2027 subscription revenue $1.40B (+27%); Q1 FY2027 $1.32B (+26%)

businessLines.name: Professional services
businessLines.how: One-time fees for incident response and security consulting, often the first contact that leads to a subscription.

brands.name: Falcon Flex
brands.note: Committed-spend contracts; $2.29B ARR at Q2 FY2027 (+101%)
